column8: - v1.4 aligns SANS Critical AI Security Guidelines with OWASP AI Exchange so both use the same control taxonomy · - AI adoption is already embedded in enterprise products; blocking AI use is not a viable security control · - Public models, shared datasets, and third-party hosting create supply-chain paths for backdoors and poisoned artifacts · - Zero model trust: models cannot be fully trusted; external controls, validation, and guardrails are required at runtime · - Agentic systems chain tools and actions; scope creep without explicit constraints is a primary deployment risk
column9: - Unauthenticated access to AI APIs or front-ends must not be allowed unless strictly necessary and monitored · - Augmentation data (system prompts, RAG context, vector DB content) must be treated as sensitive and access-controlled for read and write · - Sensitive data must be sanitized or anonymized before LLM incorporation; avoid commingling across trust boundaries · - Guardrails cannot be treated as infallible; high-stakes actions and irreversible agent calls require human oversight or escalation · - AIBOM disclosure must be restricted; technical supply-chain details aid adversaries if widely published
column10: - Map controls to eight categories: Conventional Security, Data Minimization/Obfuscation, AI Supply Chain, Data/Model Engineering, Limit Model Behavior, Model I/O Handling, Monitoring, GRC · - Apply access controls to inference endpoints, model parameters, augmentation data, and training data using least privilege · - Vet public models manually; host approved models in an internal model garden; maintain AIBOM alongside SBOM practices · - Preprocess prompts and postprocess outputs; segregate user input from system context; rate-limit interactions · - Register models centrally; monitor inference, drift, and outputs; red-team and pen-test AI infrastructure on a schedule
